newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: 40 casualties in Sri Lanka rebel raid-officials.
newsitem.headline: 40 casualties in Sri Lanka rebel raid-officials.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels attacked a remote security post in southeastern Sri Lanka on Wednesday, killing or injuring at least 40 policemen and soldiers in the biggest firefight in more than two months, officials said.

At least 10 police commandos and soldiers from the army's artillery division were killed in the battle at Pulukunava, about 200 kilometres (125 miles) east of Colombo, local security force officials said.
A military spokesman in Colombo told Reuters at least 40 men were injured in the clash, which began about 1 a.m. (1900 Tuesday GMT) and was continuing Wednesday morning.
"Reinforcements have managed to enter the camp. We will only know of our losses now," he said.
There was no immediate word on rebel casualties, and the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) could not be contacted for comment.
Security officials said the camp was occupied by about 120 men.
It was the biggest clash since September when the military pushed the Tigers out of their Kilinochchi base, 285 kilometres (180 miles) north of Colombo.

The Defence Ministry said 229 soldiers died in the assault on Kilinochchi and about 300 were wounded. It also said almost 700 Tigers were killed and more than 700 wounded, but the LTTE said only about 90 of its fighters died.

Colombo has scored a series of victories over the Tigers, including taking the rebels' northern Jaffna stronghold, after stepping up its military campaign following the breakdown of peace talks last year.
The Tigers are fighting for an independent homeland for Tamils, most of who are Hindu, in the north and the east of this predominantly Buddhist Sinhalese nation.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers insist the death toll is much higher.
